statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, *Cohen–Macaulay* means that every local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ has depth equal to Krull dimension. A complex $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is represented by a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with the self-duality isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a flat finite-presentation morphism $f:X\to Y$, *Cohen–Macaulay at $x$* means the local ring of the fibre $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Cohen–Macaulay. Let $X$ be locally Noetherian and $D_X$ a dualizing complex. Then: (1) $X$ is Cohen–Macaulay iff every point admits an open neighbourhood on which $D_X$ has exactly one nonzero cohomology sheaf; (2) for each $x$, $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Cohen–Macaulay iff the stalk $(D_X)_x$ has exactly one nonzero cohomology module; (3) the Cohen–Macaulay locus $U=\{x:\mathcal O_{X,x}\text{ is CM}\}$ is open and is Cohen–Macaulay. If $X$ is also connected and Cohen–Macaulay, there is a *single* integer $n$ and a coherent Cohen–Macaulay sheaf $\omega_X=H^n(D_X)$ with $D_X\simeq\omega_X[-n]$.

conclusions: Three CM characterizations, openness of CM locus, and single-shift dualizing sheaf on connected CM schemes.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-dualizing-module-CM-scheme}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme with dualizing complex
$\omega_X^\bullet$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is Cohen-Macaulay $\Leftrightarrow$ $\omega_X^\bullet$
locally has a unique nonzero cohomology sheaf,
\item $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is Cohen-Macaulay $\Leftrightarrow$
$\omega_{X, x}^\bullet$ has a unique nonzero cohomology,
\item $U = \{x \in X \mid \mathcal{O}_{X, x}\text{ is Cohen-Macaulay}\}$
is open and Cohen-Macaulay.
\end{enumerate}
If $X$ is connected and Cohen-Macaulay, then there is an integer $n$
and a coherent Cohen-Macaulay $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\omega_X$
such that $\omega_X^\bullet = \omega_X[-n]$.

statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, *Cohen–Macaulay* means that every local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ has depth equal to Krull dimension. A complex $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is represented by a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with the self-duality isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a flat finite-presentation morphism $f:X\to Y$, *Cohen–Macaulay at $x$* means the local ring of the fibre $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Cohen–Macaulay. Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and the category $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ of separated finite-type $S$-schemes. For $f:X\to Y$ therein, let $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ be the upper-shriek functor built from the right adjoint to proper pushforward on a compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\to Y$. In particular $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is a coherent bounded complex when $f$ is perfect. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, and $x\in X$. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) the fibre-local ring $\mathcal O_{X_{f(x)},x}$ is Cohen–Macaulay; (2) there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ on which $f^!\mathcal O_Y|_U$ is quasi-isomorphic to a *single* coherent cohomology sheaf placed in one cohomological degree (the degree may depend on $U$). In particular this is a neighbourhood statement about the relative dualizing complex, not just its single stalk.
hypotheses: f flat separated finite-type between S-schemes and point x.
conclusions: CM at x iff relative upper-shriek structure complex locally has only one nonzero cohomology sheaf.
